title: Vector-rank latency & dim breadcrumbs
content:
Purpose: messy scratchpad to capture everything while triaging several sporadic failures on /v1/rerank (hosted) and the private rerank worker farm. Want to capture commands, quick repros, hypotheses, and small tests so I don't forget the flakey bits.

Symptoms observed (summary):
- Intermittent 500s from rerank endpoint when query traffic spikes (~>200 req/s).
- When 500s happen, logs often include a dimension error from the embed->score stage: 'Dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1280' or matmul shape errors. Not every 500 has that message.
- Latency p95 spikes from ~80ms to 700ms for rerank-only requests. CPU on workers jumps and GPU utilization drops (weird).
- In private deployment, one host showed high syscall waits (iowait) during incidents.

Timeline notes (local obs):
- 2026-03-18: first user report (CS) about slow results and occasional blank reranks.
- 2026-03-19: reproduced locally with stress script (see below) but only after ~30s of sustained concurrency.
- 2026-03-21: rolled a hotfix to force-check dims earlier; reduced frequency but didn't eliminate.

Commands/traces I ran (copyable):
- quick stress client: python -c "import requests,threading; s=lambda:requests.post('https://api.redwood/re-rank', json={'qid':'x','cands':["txt"]*50}); [threading.Thread(target=s).start() for _ in range(250)]"
- capture failing trace (curl wrapper): curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood/re-rank -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @payload.json --max-time 10 2>&1 | tee /tmp/rerank-curl.log
- inside worker: sudo perf top -p $(pgrep rerank_worker) during spike -> heavy time in python GC/lock_acquire (suspicious)
- lower-level: gdb attach to worker and thread apply all bt -> saw threads stuck on _PyEval_EvalFrameDefault in several frames where matrix ops happen
- quick py repro: python - <<PY
import numpy as np
q = np.random.rand(1,1280)
c = np.random.rand(50,1536)
# matmul will raise
try:
  print(q @ c.T)
except Exception as e:
  print('ERR', e)
PY
- Confirmed: mismatch raises ValueError: shapes (1,1280) and (1536,50) not aligned

Logs (snippets):
- 2026-03-19T14:32:12Z rerank_worker[pid=3121] ERROR scoring.py:142 "Dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1280"
- 2026-03-19T14:32:12Z rerank_worker[pid=3121] DEBUG request-id=abc123 payload-cand-count=50 topk=10
- 2026-03-19T14:32:12Z rerank_worker[pid=3121] INFO fallback-policy=rank-only
- 2026-03-21T09:11:04Z rerank_worker[pid=4120] WARN healthcheck p95_latency=723ms

Hypotheses (brainstorm):
1) Upstream producer (embedding service) sometimes responds with smaller-dim vectors (1280) when using a different model variant (quantized / older version) and the rerank worker doesn't validate dims early enough. Race window: model swap + cached manifest leads to mixing dims.
2) Vector indexing backend (FAISS) returns ids and we fetch embeddings lazily from cache; stale cache entries are from old indexing run (different dim).
3) Memory corruption or shape inference bug in numpy/torch when running batched matmuls under high concurrency -> leads to reading wrong buffer shape (less likely but can't rule out).
4) Serialization bug across RPC boundary: our proto schema doesn't encode dim, code assumes fixed dim and trusts shape from bytes; if sender truncates padded vectors you get smaller arrays.
5) Backpressure/backoff misconfiguration in the router: when overloaded we merge payloads (i.e., combine candidate lists wrongly) producing ragged arrays passed down.

Quick experiments to differentiate hypotheses:
- Test A: explicit dim-check at earliest possible boundary (right after unpacking RPC) and log sender model-id + vector-length. If we see model ids != expected when dims mismatch => hypothesis 1 or 4. (We did a short roll; frequency dropped.)
- Test B: force re-index and invalidate embedding cache on a single node, then replay the same workload. If issue disappears -> cache/index mismatch (hypothesis 2).
- Test C: run with numpy-build replaced by MKL vs OpenBLAS to see whether matmul misbehaves under load (hypothesis 3).
- Test D: enable stricter proto checks in client/server (length prefix + expected_dim field) to catch truncation (hypothesis 4).

What I tried and results:
- Added fast dim-check in unpack path (hotfix 2026-03-21): logs now show more details: for mismatches we saw sender_model_tag values varying between 'redwood-embed-v2' (1536) and 'redwood-embed-v1-1280' (1280). That strongly supports hypothesis 1 (model variant mixing).
- Replayed traffic after forcing the router to pin requests to a single embed cluster instance (no autopromote): mismatch events dropped to near zero.
- In private infra instance that still had incidents, confirmed older model binary present in /opt/models/embedding-old. There is a deployment path that can leave the old binary around if cleanup fails.

Root-cause theory (current):
- During a rolling model upgrade, some Embed nodes served the old model (1280) while others served the new one (1536). The rerank pipeline assumed a stable embedding dimension per-customer and didn't validate consistently early, so occasionally a query would fetch embeddings from different model variants (e.g., query embedding produced by v2 but candidate embeddings from a shard still holding v1), causing matmul/dim errors. Overload exacerbates because routing/fanout increases chance of mixing sources.

Open questions: 
- Why does GPU utilization drop when CPU climbs? My guess: crashed GPU kernels fall back to CPU matmul in some codepath (or we abort and re-run CPU scoring) — need to confirm with nvprof.
- How often are clients/responses using an explicit model tag vs implicit? Need to standardize model/version tags in proto.
- Is there a latent bug in the indexer that allows old-v1 embeddings to be read after a reindex?

Short-term mitigations implemented: 
- Implemented strict dimension check as fail-safe and added telemetry counter: rerank.dim_mismatch.count.
- Router change: pin per-query fanout to a consistent embed cluster for the duration of request. Rollout to 20% traffic.
- Quick CI job added to test upgrade path: deploy embed v2 -> run synthetic traffic -> force-reindex -> check for any v1 reads.

Longer-term follow-ups (todo):
- Make model-version explicit in embedding proto (fields: model_name, model_hash, dims) and fail early on mismatch. Add a migration plan. (Jira RI-4021).
- Harden deploy cleanup to ensure old model binaries removed and index versions incremented atomically.
- Add e2e chaos test: random embed node restarts + rolling swaps while stress client runs to reproduce mixing.
- Investigate GPU drop: gather nvprof traces during a spike.

Small reproduction recipe (local):
1) start two local embed servers: one serving 1280-dim model (serve: --model embed-v1 --dim 1280) and one 1536 (serve: --model embed-v2 --dim 1536).
2) start rerank worker that doesn't check dims (use old container).
3) run stress client that fans out to both embed servers and sends many queries.
4) observe some requests failing with dimension errors after ~30s.

Notes-to-self:
- When writing logs for mismatches include request-id, sender node, model-tag, embed-dim, candidate-shard-id. Track patterns per shard.
- Add a nightly scan job that validates index dims across clusters and fails if mismatch found.
- Talk to infra about automating 'remove-old-models' step in deployment pipeline; it looks like a leftover from earlier experiment.

Next immediate steps I will do (this week):
- Finish proto change PR draft and post to eng-applied-ml for review (high priority).
- Add nvprof capture to the incident runbook and try to capture GPU trace during next spike.
- Run chaos e2e on staging with pinned traces to try and reproduce deterministically.
- Sync with Jonah + Marta tomorrow 10am PT to go over telemetry dashboards (rerank.dim_mismatch.count, per-model-serving-counts).

Random misc scratch lines:
- weird: sometimes mismatch logged but request still returns valid ranked list (maybe mismatch occurs in fallback scoring path but we continue).
- consider embedding length padding as temporary compatibility layer (pad 1280->1536) but that risks semantic degradation — only for emergency mode.

End of notes.
